newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones to expand, revitalize Telerate.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones to expand, revitalize Telerate.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co Monday said it planned to invest up to $650 million over the next 36 to 48 months to expand and revitalize Dow Jones Telerate, the company's global financial information services unit.
The company estimated that after the Telerate costs, 1997 earnings will be between $1.20 and $1.40 per share. Earnings in 1998 also will be affected by the program.
The Telerate investment will be funded mostly out of operating cash flow, and Dow Jones does not expect to incur a significant amount of additional debt to finance the program, it said.
Dow Jones also reported fourth-quarter share earnings of $0.62, even with a year ago. Dow Jones stock lost 1-1/2 to 39-3/8.
According to First Call, the Street's consensus for the latest quarter was $0.60 and $1.94 for 1997.

"This investment program represents a bold and cohesive strategy for Dow Jones Telerate that will significantly enhance Dow Jones' long-term shareholder value and benefit our customers," said Peter Kann, chairman and chief executive.
"Dow Jones Telerate is a successful business and participates in a growing global information industry. It has experienced some slowdown recently, and we mean to remedy that," he added.

Dow Jones Telerate, one of Dow Jones' largest business units, will be expanded to provide the financial institutions with an array of information and services for trading, analysis, research, risk management and transactions in major market segments, Dow Jones said. Plans call for enhancements to Dow Jones Telerate's services and network; a reorganization around market segments; and new partnership programs for customers in the global fixed income, equities, foreign exchange, commodities and energy markets.
